author: white-axe
body:
This pull request adds libretro builds to mkxp-z, which can be used in libretro frontends such as RetroArch.

Since RetroArch supports a lot of platforms, I was able to add support for a few extra platforms:

- Android
- Emscripten
- iOS
- Nintendo Switch
- PlayStation 4
- webOS

I've also added several other game console builds, but they don't work yet since they have no OpenGL support. I'll add a software renderer eventually for those consoles, but in the meantime, these non-functional console builds exist solely to make sure that no one breaks them.

Also, the libretro builds have save state support, which allows you to save and restore the state of the game engine whenever you want. Save states are 100% portable across different operating systems and CPU architectures; as for endianness, save states get saved in native endianness and the machine loading them performs byte swapping when loading if applicable. RetroArch's rewind feature is supported but requires disabling "Threaded Audio" in the core options because RetroArch doesn't support rewinding unless the audio is rendered from the main thread. Manual saving and loading of save states doesn't require disabling "Threaded Audio".

To try out a libretro build on a non-Emscripten, non-iOS platform, download the relevant core from the autobuild and put it wherever your libretro frontend keeps all the other cores. If you're using RetroArch and haven't updated your core info files in the RetroArch online updater since 2025-12-07, also use the online updater to update the core info files since that's around the time when I added the core info file for mkxp-z to RetroArch.

To test out the Emscripten build, I have it hosted at https://white-axe.github.io/mkxp-z-libretro-emscripten/.

For iOS, you need to manually build the frontend as described [here](https://docs.libretro.com/development/retroarch/compilation/ios/).

To run a game, you have several options:

- Load the Game.ini or mkxp.json as the game.
- Create an empty file with the file extension .rxproj, .rvproj or .rvproj2 in the same directory as Game.ini and/or mkxp.json, and load that as the game. This is intended to make it easier to deal with save states in RetroArch, since RetroArch's save states are named after the file you load as the game, so if you load Game.ini or mkxp.json, all the save states for every game will be named "Game" or "mkxp", which is really inconvenient.
- Put the game into a zip or 7z archive with file extension .mkxpz, .zip or .7z and load that as the game. Please note that the files inside the zip or 7z archive should be uncompressed if possible, especially .rgssad/.rgss2a/.rgss3a and .otf/.ttf files inside the archive, or the game will lag quite a bit from trying to seek compressed files.

There are a few differences between libretro builds and standalone builds:

- Every filesystem call made from Ruby is routed through a virtual filesystem with the following paths:
  - /Game - A directory with read-write permissions that represents the game directory, whatever RTPs the game uses, and the save directory all union mounted together (the save directory union mounting is for games that save to the current working directory). Files written to this path are always written to the save directory, not the game directory or RTP directories. The current working directory is always set to /Game when the game starts up.
  - /Save - A directory with read-write permissions that represents just the save directory without the union mounting with the game directory. The function `System.data_directory` returns "/Save/" in libretro builds.
  - /System/RTP - A directory with read-only permissions where RTPs are loaded from. This directory is physically located at \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/System/RTP.
  - /System/Fonts - A directory with read-only permissions where fonts are loaded from as a fallback if they aren't found in /Game/Fonts. This directory is physically located at \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/System/Fonts.
  - /System/Scripts/Preload - A directory with read-only permissions where preload scripts that can be selected in the core options are read from. This is the directory \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/Scripts/Preload. In addition, the three preload scripts provided in this repository are union mounted with it so that those preload scripts are usable without the user having to manually copy them here.
  - /System/Scripts/Postload - A directory with read-only permissions where postload scripts that can be selected in the core options are read from. This is the directory \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/Scripts/Postload.
  - /Dist - A directory with read-only permissions that includes all the scripts and whatnot that Ruby needs to actually start up successfully. This directory is physically a zip file built during stage 1 of the libretro build, embedded in the libretro core and read directly from memory at runtime.
- RTP paths in mkxp.json are relative to /System/RTP instead of the game directory.
- RTPs set in Game.ini are loaded in libretro builds in addition to the ones specified in mkxp.json; they also get loaded from /System/RTP.
- The `System.platform` function always returns "libretro". All of the `System.is_` functions return false, except for a new `System.is_libretro?` function that returns true.
- The Ruby version has been changed to 3.3.10, because the build process used by the libretro cores is only supported by Ruby 3.2 and later and there are some bugs in the WASI builds of Ruby older than Ruby 3.3. I can change it to another version if you want, but it has to be at least 3.2.

A few things that I have yet to implement in the future:

- There are several console builds that don't work yet because they don't have OpenGL support. I'll eventually add a software renderer for those.
- ~~Loading preload scripts is not implemented yet. I'll likely attempt to use the libretro cheats interface to handle loading preload scripts.~~ Loading preload and postload scripts is now implemented. Any scripts in /System/Scripts/Preload or /System/Scripts/Postload can be enabled and disabled in the core options. Preload and postload scripts specified in mkxp.json will be loaded in addition to the ones specified in the core options; the preload scripts in mkxp.json will be loaded after the preload scripts specified in the core options, and the postload scripts in mkxp.json will be loaded before the postload scripts specified in the core options.
- Save states are currently unable to save and restore the positions of MIDI BGM tracks because seeking MIDI tracks is not implemented in the audio backend. I'll implement seeking for MIDI tracks to fix this.
- There is OpenGL support for the PlayStation Vita, but it requires all shaders to be written in a different language than GLSL. Other than that, though, everything else should be the same as normal OpenGL, so this most likely just needs a compiler that can convert the GLSL shaders to whatever format the Vita driver needs, or manual conversion of the shaders.
- Apparently, some devices that have PowerVR GPUs, in particular the PlayStation Vita but also some Android devices, have a limited number of OpenGL FBOs available. This is a problem, since mkxp-z uses one FBO per texture. I'll probably fix this by detecting if the device has a PowerVR GPU, and, if this is the case, changing the rendering to use a few global FBOs that are bound to textures when needed, and retaining the old method otherwise for better performance.
- I can also add builds for some Xbox consoles, which luckily have OpenGL support (via ANGLE). I'm pretty sure these require MSVC, though, so it might be tricky.

### Description

In https://github.com/metabase/metabase/pull/51929 we moved the collection permission check into a CTE to prevent it from being run multiple times to improve the performance of getting all the collections a user has permission to see. However we didn't move the effective-children subquery to use this cte since the query to get them needs to check the permissions of each 'effective' child as well are parents of the child collection to build this query.

author: samd2021
body:
This Pull Request introduces support for deploying RHEL Image Mode on DPUs, with an initial focus on Intel IPUs. This feature is critical for the future of RHEL deployments on edge devices, as RHEL 9.6 deprecates the RHEL for Edge OSTree deployment model, and RHEL 10 makes RHEL Image Mode Generally Available while removing RHEL for Edge artifacts entirely. RHEL Image Mode is set to be the sole official edge deployment model for RHEL 10 and subsequent releases.
For our use case, there are some good benefits and a few caveats to tackle:
Benefits:
- Remove Arm server requirements by targeting aarch64 on x86 hosts for both the ISO and day 0 and day 2 operations
- Brings automation from Kickstart and CDA into the RHEL deployment on first boot
- Reuse cloud native technologies and workflow throughout the pipeline (Openshift, Podman and Podman desktop, container registries, etc).
Current Caveats for our special use case:
- RHSM introduces problems when doing cross arch RHEL image mode builds because of host arch specific entitlements, (Building the container in openshift/kind clusters with Konflux ci seems to fix these issues)
- We require grub Kernel arguments at ISO time so we have a workaround to inject it. I am working with upstream to fix this in osbuild/bootc-image-builder#899

Changes that touch original behavior:
- Made auth.py more reusable to enable private container registries for image mode as well as the CI registry.
- Made `Result` iterable for easier UX without touching original behavior.
- Added an image_mode config to be able to pass information necessary to build the ISO

# Description
This feature implements a  timesheet approval system that allows supervisors to view, review, and approve pending timesheet days from employees in their company

# Main Changes
- Added `PendingApprovalWithEmployeeInfo` model to combine approval data with employee information
- Added `GET /api/approval/pending-by-employee-with-info` endpoint that returns pending approvals with employee details
- Extended `TimesheetRepository` with queries for pending approvals
- New queries and commands for day approval
- Timesheet approval view
- **Schema Updates** (`033-alter-days-add-submission-fields.sql`):
  - Added `IsSubmitted` field to track submission status
  - Added `LastSubmitTimestamp` field to track when days were last submitted
- **Automatic Submission Trigger** (`034-create-trigger-auto-submit-day.sql`):
  - Automatically marks days as submitted when hours or description are updated
  
# Motivation and Context
Previously, there was no way for supervisors to review and approve employee timesheet entries

# How to Test
1. Run the following database scripts in order:
   ```sql
   033-alter-days-add-submission-fields.sql
   034-create-trigger-auto-submit-day.sql
   ```
2. Run backend and frontend
3. Log in as an employee
4. Enter hours and descriptions for timesheet days
5. Verify that the trigger automatically sets `IsSubmitted = 1`
6. Log in as a supervisor
7. Navigate to the Timesheet Approvals view (/timesheet-approvals)
8. Verify you only see employees from your company
9. Click "Ver detalles" to open the approval modal
10. Approve individual days and verify they're removed from pending list
11. Create employees in different companies
12. Verify supervisors only see their company's employees

#546: General Names (SAN, AKI, IAN, CDP) - remove sorting

Users can define their own order, so we don't need to sort automatically.
Ideally, we can provide a way to reorder items in future (up and down arrows to move records across the table).

**Important observation**
- there is a potential issue - "General Name" column is sortable, so users can add sorting on the column, but sorting doesn't affect the final saved result (say you created records "a", "c", "b" and after that sorted DESC -> resulting to "c", "b", "a"; but on pressing "OK", model still has "a", "c", "b", so user may be confused)
- it's not difficult to fix (e.g. we can add "RowSortListener" for the table sorter), but I would think twice before doing that for reasons:
  - I'm not sure if users would really expect that sorted results will be saved - usually, sorting doesn't impact saved data
  - probably, the easiest option would be just to remove sorting feature from "General Name" column
- issue with sorting exists even in current version (without the fix) - we can sort DESC, but data will be sort in ascending order

author: squadgazzz
body:
# Description
An issue was recently observed where the settlement queue remained full for a long period of time. That was caused by a stuck current block stream, which blocked the settlement task in the driver. While the autopilot had already aborted the `/settle` request, due to the nature of the async settlement operation, it continued to execute until the current block stream was recovered. During that time, the settlement queue could no longer accept any additional requests.

One possible(and very trivial) option to address it is to set a next block awaiting timeout, but that covers only this specific async operation, where many more potentially can block the queue. This PR introduces a mechanism to detect whether the `/settle` request is dropped, which cancels the settlement task and also stops the internal loop that awaits the settlement tx.

# Changes
In the function that receives a new settlement execution request from the settlement queue, a `response_sender` is already provided, which is used as a channel to return results to the `/settle` endpoint caller. When the client drops the request, the `response_receiver` is also dropped. This can be detected by awaiting the `response_sender.closed()` execution. This exact event is used as a cancellation signal for the settlement task. The task will be finished and removed from the settlement queue.

For a reference, a place where the response sender and receiver are initialized. So, dropping `response_receiver` will trigger the implemented signal:
https://github.com/cowprotocol/services/blob/79b129f41891393743d1789a59e98da7f492e6f1/crates/driver/src/domain/competition/mod.rs#L341-L368

## How to test
That seems to be very tricky, so probably ensuring it works properly in staging should be enough.

## Summary

This PR implements comprehensive MCP (Model Context Protocol) server support for the CLI utility, enabling users to extend the agent's capabilities with external tools and resources.

## Key Features Implemented

### Core Infrastructure
- **Type Definitions**: Complete TypeScript type system for MCP operations
- **Connection Management**: Both stdio and SSE-based server connections
- **Service Layer**: `CLIMcpService` for centralized MCP operations
- **Configuration System**: JSON-based configuration with validation

### CLI Commands
- `roo mcp list` - List configured MCP servers and their status
- `roo mcp connect <server-id>` - Connect to an MCP server
- `roo mcp disconnect <server-id>` - Disconnect from an MCP server
- `roo mcp tools [server-id]` - List available tools from connected servers
- `roo mcp resources [server-id]` - List available resources
- `roo mcp execute <server-id> <tool-name> [args...]` - Execute MCP tools
- `roo mcp config init` - Initialize MCP configuration
- `roo mcp config validate` - Validate configuration
- `roo mcp config show` - Show current configuration

### Technical Implementation

#### Server Connection Classes
- `StdioMcpConnection` - Handles stdio-based MCP servers
- `SseMcpConnection` - Handles SSE-based MCP servers
- Health checking and automatic reconnection
- Proper error handling and cleanup

#### Service Layer
- Server discovery and capability detection
- Tool and resource enumeration
- Parameter validation for tool execution
- Configuration file management
- Connection lifecycle management

#### CLI Integration
- New CLI options for MCP configuration
- Help documentation and examples
- Proper error messaging and user feedback
- Support for multiple output formats

## Configuration

The system supports a `~/.roo/mcp-config.json` file with example configurations for popular MCP servers:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "servers": [
    {
      "id": "github-server",
      "name": "GitHub MCP Server",
      "type": "stdio",
      "enabled": true,
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    }
  ],
  "defaults": {
    "timeout": 30000,
    "retryAttempts": 3,
    "autoConnect": true
  }
}
```

## Testing

Comprehensive unit tests cover:
- All connection types and error scenarios
- Service layer functionality
- Configuration validation
- Tool execution and parameter handling
- Health checking and lifecycle management

## Files Added/Modified

### New Files
- `src/cli/types/mcp-types.ts` - Core MCP type definitions
- `src/cli/types/mcp-config-types.ts` - Configuration types and examples
- `src/cli/connections/StdioMcpConnection.ts` - Stdio connection implementation
- `src/cli/connections/SseMcpConnection.ts` - SSE connection implementation
- `src/cli/services/CLIMcpService.ts` - Main service implementation
- `src/cli/commands/mcp-commands.ts` - CLI command implementations
- `src/cli/services/__tests__/CLIMcpService.test.ts` - Service tests
- `src/cli/connections/__tests__/StdioMcpConnection.test.ts` - Stdio tests
- `src/cli/connections/__tests__/SseMcpConnection.test.ts` - SSE tests

### Modified Files
- `src/cli/index.ts` - Added MCP CLI options and command registration

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Initialize MCP configuration
roo-cli mcp config init

# List configured servers
roo-cli mcp list

# Connect to a server
roo-cli mcp connect github-server

# List available tools
roo-cli mcp tools

# Execute a tool
roo-cli mcp execute github-server get_repo owner=user repo=project

# List resources
roo-cli mcp resources github-server
```

## Quality Assurance

✅ **Build**: All builds pass successfully  
✅ **Lint**: Code follows project style guidelines  
✅ **Types**: Full TypeScript type coverage  
✅ **Tests**: Comprehensive unit test coverage  
✅ **Documentation**: Complete CLI help and examples

- Story #15: Integrate MCP Server Support
- Implements all acceptance criteria from the story
- Provides foundation for extending CLI with external MCP servers

None - This is a purely additive feature.

## Future Enhancements

- Auto-discovery of local MCP servers
- GUI configuration management
- Advanced tool parameter validation
